summary.name: Pixilation (supplemental design reference; not a directly named source-collection style)
summary.visualIdentity: Live performers are photographed pose by pose, so motion advances in deliberate stepped positions while scene and costume stay continuous. It is not pixel art and not ordinary low-frame-rate footage. Provenance is supplemental.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly suited to surreal performance pieces used alone, music videos, energetic social campaigns, and event promos pairing kinetic type. Inferred: other performer-led stepped narratives. Unspecified: non-human subjects and explanatory content.
summary.limitations: Requires photographed human performers; no listed renderer exists. Stepped pose timing cannot be replaced by low-fps footage or smooth tweens, and ordinary low-frame-rate footage must not be described as authentic pixilation. Avoid beat flashing, continuity breaks, and covering faces. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
summary.palette: Example tokens only, with no approved exact colors supplied: background #EEE7DC, foreground #343C43, accent #8A9288. Background policy is scene_dependent, so choose the canvas from the scene rather than defaulting to this swatch. Apply tokens only to new presentation elements; costumes, environment, and lighting stay unchanged. Foreground on background measures 9.127:1 for body text; accent on foreground at 3.495:1 is decorative only. Gradients are disabled. The source frame review found no sufficiently strong match in the 1–8 second samples.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Motion is stepped exposure: performers slide, jump unexpectedly, and interact with objects, with readable direction and exposure holds. Exposure rate may differ from delivery rate, and interpolated in-between poses should not be added automatically. Optional references motion-012 (chapter handoff) and motion-015 (story steps) are screened and may be omitted. Interactive HTML may use an image-sequence player with pause and reduced-motion stills.
summary.audio: No audio is mandated; the source leaves music, voiceover, sung vocals, effects, ambience, and silence open. Inferred suggestion: beat-aligned music for music-driven pieces, with longer exposures at section changes. Genre, tempo, voice, and language are unspecified. Silence is valid where reading holds need space.
summary.assetRequirements: Photographed performer pose frames are required as numbered sequences with alpha, consistent dimensions, and a clear layer manifest. Costume and lighting continuity must come from the shoot itself. Local fonts must load before rendering. No uploads are supplied in this metadata. Any audio must be task-provided, authorized, or created locally.
summary.combinations: style-105 supplies beat-aligned timing: pose jumps land on a verified beat table, with longer holds at section changes. style-093 supplies kinetic type stepping on photo exposures, using #343C43 text and #8A9288 accent only, with clear reading holds. Avoid smooth tweens over stepped footage, covering faces, and spring motion on every letter. Use alone for surreal performance.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default pipeline for composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export, using one paused GSAP timeline registered per composition. Remotion is fallback only when a recorded verified limitation applies; an existing React project is not a reason. Photographed frames serve as the style renderer and stepped exposure timing as the motion engine, since recommended stack references are empty. FFmpeg encodes at the intended rate; Python and chroma-js are optional supporting tools.
